text:
Sara: Heads up — jerboa-v1 int8 bringup shows a couple of locale regressions: CJK token boundary shifts in zh/ja and bracket mirroring for ar/rtl. attaching small repro and metrics.
Jun: ok can you paste a failing sample?
Sara: sure — short repro:
Sara: zh input: "商品说明(改进版)"
Sara: jerboa-v1 int8 detok: "商品 说明改进 版 )"  <-- missing isolation space and trailing bracket wrong side for rtl samples
Liam: :eyes: that looks like a token boundary shift, similar to what we saw after the kernel reorder last week
Maria: quick metrics snapshot: WMT-zh-en BLEU -0.7, chrF -2.3 on shortctx subset; multilingual-embed-bench cosine -0.08 (embedding drift)
Chen: can you paste token ids / diff?
Sara: token ids diff snippet:
```
- ... 102, 3456, 78, 999
+ ... 102, 3456, 778, 999
```
Sara: see that +? a subtoken fused differently -> boundary shifted
Jun: repro command I used:
```
python -m eval.run --model jerboa-v1 --quant int8 --samples tests/locale/zh_jp_samples.json --detok-mode strict
```
Jun: I ran that locally — tokenmap appears offset for vocab range 3450-3800 when precompilation order changed
Chen: db2f9a9 touched tokenizer precompilation ordering on release branch — suspect culprit
Maria: note: fp16 -> int8 shows same boundary shift, so quantization alone isn't the root cause
Liam: could still be combination (tokenmap + kernel reorder) exposing nondeterminism in subtoken merging
Sara: Eval-bot CI summary: guardrail failed 12/2000 samples (0.6%) threshold 0.2% — failing mostly CJK short-ctx and mixed JP-kana cases
Eval-bot: scheduled full run 3188889000 (50k samples) to collect full matrix (tokenmap rollback x kernel pins)
Jun: quick mitigation idea: post-detok normalize CJK punctuation spacing and force bracket reorientation on rtl responses until we fix upstream
Sara: temporary patch I tested (python):
```
# post-detok quickfix
s = re.sub(r'([\u4e00-\u9fff])(\(|\))', r'\1 \2', s)
if is_rtl:
    s = s.replace('(', '（').replace(')', '）')
```
Sara: ugly but reduces customer-visible regressions in smoke set
Liam: mitigate is fine short-term, but we need a proper bisect and fix — can someone run a git-bisect with db2f9a9 as first bad?
Chen: starting bisect now, will test tokenmap-only rollback and then kernel pin combos
Maria: plan: (1) bisect to confirm offending commit(s) (2) run full eval matrix (50k) with tokenmap rollback and kernel pins (3) create unit tests in locale-detok for the failing patterns (4) revert/patch as needed
Jun: adding test vectors to tests/locale: zh_jp_bracket_edgecases.json and arabic_bracket_flip.json
Sara: FYI Dedicated customers might have pinned older runtimes — flagging @oncall and @eng-runtime to watch for increased error rates during rollout
Liam: any quick sample showing rtl bracket mirror?
Sara: arabic input: "قائمة (عينة)" -> jerboa detok: "قائمة )عينة(" (brackets flipped and glued)
Jun: that mirror definitely points at bidi reordering + detok mismatch, likely token sequence order changed
Chen: bisect update: first-pass ruled out tokenizer vocab build; second-pass shows ordering change in precomp step introduced a non-deterministic mapping when parallelized (commit db2f9a9 changed threading order)
Maria: OK we have root cause hypothesis = precomp ordering + kernel reorder nondeterminism. next steps are reproducible patch + unit tests + revert candidate if needed.
Sara: I'll open a PR with the post-detok mitigation and unit tests and link the bisect notes. tagging @eng-ml-leads for prioritization.
Liam: thanks — keep the thread updated, will coordinate rollback window if bisect confirms bad commit.
Sara: thx everyone :thumbsup:
